'''Mapia''' is an extinct<ref>{{Cite web |last=((Desk)) |first=((News)) |title=Four Papuan languages extinct, linguist says - Archipelago |url=https://www.thejakartapost.com/indonesia/2024/02/22/four-papuan-languages-extinct-linguist-says.html |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=The Jakarta Post |language=en}}</ref> [[Micronesian languages|Micronesian language]], the only one spoken in Indonesia. It was spoken on [[Mapia Atoll]], 180 km north of the coast of [[New Guinea]], part of [[Supiori Regency]]. The population emigrated early in the 20th century,<ref name="ethnologue">{{cite web |title=Mapia |url=http://www.ethnologue.com/language/mpy/ |website=Ethnologue |publisher=SIL International | edition = 25 |accessdate=5 December 2022}}</ref> the only speaker as of 2000 was an elderly man who had remained behind on the island.{{Citation needed|date=December 2022}} The rest of the population of Mapia are now [[Biak language|Biak]]-speaking immigrants.
